source: /data/use-of-english/ (the Master page's own items, so a mistake on the Board and on the page is one mistake)

rounds.prompt: Mia has always been brilliant ___ anything involving numbers, so nobody was surprised when she chose to study engineering.
rounds.note: Brilliant / good at something. Good with numbers is also right.

rounds.prompt: After months of planning, we are really looking forward ___ finally getting on the plane.
rounds.note: Look forward to + -ing: to is a preposition here, so the verb takes -ing.

rounds.prompt: Daniel arrived forty minutes after the start. He apologised ___ keeping everyone waiting and blamed the traffic.
rounds.note: Apologise for (doing) something.

rounds.prompt: Whether we hold the barbecue in the garden or not will depend ___ the weather on the day.
rounds.note: Depend on (or upon).

rounds.prompt: Although the team lost the final, the coach said she had never been prouder ___ her players.
rounds.note: Proud of — and prouder of.

rounds.prompt: Nobody in the office was surprised ___ the news that Alex had resigned; he had been unhappy for months.
rounds.note: Surprised at or by.

rounds.prompt: We have already missed the last train, so there is no point ___ rushing to the station now.
rounds.note: There is no point in + -ing.

rounds.prompt: Lucy has become increasingly interested ___ Japanese culture since her trip to Kyoto, and she is now learning the language.
rounds.note: Interested in.

rounds.prompt: The airline has still not given passengers a reason ___ the delay, which has left hundreds of them stranded.
rounds.note: A reason for something.

rounds.prompt: Many people who are afraid ___ flying find that the fear disappears once they understand how planes work.
rounds.note: Afraid of.

rounds.prompt: In spite ___ the rain, thousands of fans stayed until the very end of the concert.
rounds.note: In spite of + noun phrase (despite has no of).

rounds.prompt: The final was postponed because ___ the storm, which had flooded part of the stadium.
rounds.note: Because of + noun phrase. Because alone needs a clause.

rounds.prompt: Why not cycle to work instead ___ sitting in traffic every morning? It is cheaper, and you will get some exercise too.
rounds.note: Instead of + -ing.

rounds.prompt: The town is famous ___ its seafood, so make sure you try the local fish while you are there.
rounds.note: Famous for.

rounds.prompt: I have not heard from Sara ___ almost a month. I hope nothing has happened to her.
rounds.note: For + a length of time (in also works after a negative).

rounds.prompt: At first glance, the new logo looks very similar ___ the old one, but the colours are slightly brighter.
rounds.note: Similar to.

rounds.prompt: In addition ___ her full-time job, Rosa volunteers at an animal shelter every weekend.
rounds.note: In addition to + noun or -ing.

rounds.prompt: I was introduced ___ my future business partner at a friend’s wedding, of all places.
rounds.note: Introduce someone to someone.

rounds.prompt: Before you start the course, it helps to be familiar ___ the basic vocabulary of economics.
rounds.note: Familiar with something you know. (Something is familiar to you.)

rounds.prompt: The bridge, which was designed ___ a team of young engineers, has won several international awards.
rounds.note: By + the agent in a passive sentence.

rounds.prompt: Strong winds prevented the ferry ___ leaving the harbour, so we spent an extra night on the island.
rounds.note: Prevent someone / something from + -ing.

rounds.prompt: ___ to a recent survey, most teenagers spend more than four hours a day online.
rounds.note: According to + a source of information.

rounds.prompt: ___ from a few minor delays, the whole trip went exactly as we had planned.
rounds.note: Apart from means except for.

rounds.prompt: My grandmother worries ___ everything, from the weather to whether we are eating properly.
rounds.note: Worry about.

rounds.prompt: After two years of general medicine, Dr Khan decided to specialise ___ children’s heart conditions.
rounds.note: Specialise in.

rounds.prompt: The old cinema in the town centre is going to be turned ___ a modern arts centre next year.
rounds.note: Turn something into something: a change of form.

rounds.prompt: We had only just set off when we ran ___ some old friends we had not seen for years.
rounds.note: Run into (or across) someone: meet them by chance.

rounds.prompt: Some students find it hard to cope ___ the pressure of exams, so the school now offers relaxation classes.
rounds.note: Cope with.

rounds.prompt: The price of a ticket has gone up ___ five euros, from twenty to twenty-five.
rounds.note: By + the size of a change: up by five euros.

rounds.prompt: The flight was full, so we were lucky to get seats at all, let alone seats next ___ each other.
rounds.note: Next to.

rounds.prompt: ___ the hotel was a long way from the beach, we really enjoyed our stay there.
rounds.note: Although + a full clause.

rounds.prompt: The match went ahead ___ the heavy rain, and both teams played remarkably well.
rounds.note: Despite + a noun phrase. Although needs a clause.

rounds.prompt: Could you text me as soon ___ you land? I want to know you have arrived safely.
rounds.note: As soon as.

rounds.prompt: Many students take a part-time job in ___ to pay for their studies.
rounds.note: In order to + infinitive: purpose.

rounds.prompt: The children were not allowed to leave the table ___ everyone had finished eating.
rounds.note: Until gives the time when something changes.

rounds.prompt: The flat is in a great location; ___, it is far too expensive for a student like me.
rounds.note: However links two contrasting ideas and takes a comma.

rounds.prompt: We will miss the start of the film ___ we leave in the next five minutes.
rounds.note: Unless means if not.

rounds.prompt: I have emailed the museum to ask ___ students can get a discount on weekdays.
rounds.note: If or whether introduces an indirect yes/no question.

rounds.prompt: He walked into the meeting an hour late and sat down as ___ nothing had happened.
rounds.note: As though or as if + past perfect for an unreal comparison.

rounds.prompt: The course teaches practical cooking skills as ___ as the basics of nutrition.
rounds.note: As well as means and also.

rounds.prompt: Some of my classmates love living in the city, ___ others cannot wait to move back to the countryside.
rounds.note: While or whereas shows a contrast between two groups.

rounds.prompt: The guide spoke slowly and clearly ___ that everyone in the group could follow her.
rounds.note: So that + clause shows purpose.

rounds.prompt: Pack a warm jumper in ___ the evenings get cold. It is often windy up in the mountains.
rounds.note: In case + clause: as a precaution.

rounds.prompt: You are welcome to borrow my camera as ___ as you promise to look after it.
rounds.note: As long as means on condition that.

rounds.prompt: Make sure you book a table in advance; ___, you might not get a seat on a Saturday night.
rounds.note: Otherwise means if you do not.

rounds.prompt: The storm meant we could not go to the beach, so we visited the aquarium ___.
rounds.note: Instead at the end means in place of the thing just mentioned.

rounds.prompt: I am not going to change my mind about the job, even ___ they offer me more money.
rounds.note: Even if + a possible future situation.

rounds.prompt: I still cannot decide ___ to study medicine or law next year.
rounds.note: Whether + to-infinitive. If cannot be used here.

rounds.prompt: ___ hard I try, I can never remember people’s names at parties.
rounds.note: However + adjective or adverb means no matter how.

rounds.prompt: It was not ___ I got home that I realised I had left my laptop on the train.
rounds.note: Not until marks the point when something first happened.

rounds.prompt: The interviewer asked me ___ I had ever worked in a team before.
rounds.note: Reported yes/no question: if or whether.

rounds.prompt: ___ I had known how busy the restaurant would be, I would have booked a table.
rounds.note: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Call me at any time ___ you need anything — even in the middle of the night.
rounds.note: If (or whenever) introduces the condition.

rounds.prompt: Not only did the new manager reduce costs, ___ she also improved staff morale.
rounds.note: Not only … but (also).

rounds.prompt: ___ the youngest of five children, Leo had to learn to stand up for himself from an early age.
rounds.note: As here means in the role or position of.

rounds.prompt: I had hardly closed my eyes ___ the phone started ringing.
rounds.note: Hardly … when (no sooner … than is the matching pair).

rounds.prompt: I wish I ___ more free time during the week; I hardly ever get to see my friends.
rounds.note: Wish + past simple for a present regret.

rounds.prompt: That cough sounds terrible. You ___ better see a doctor before it gets any worse.
rounds.note: Had better + bare infinitive: strong advice.

rounds.prompt: It was an unforgettable day for Sara. Not only ___ she win the race, but she also broke the national record.
rounds.note: Inversion after not only needs an auxiliary.

rounds.prompt: The kitchen window ___ broken by a football during the match last night, so it has to be replaced.
rounds.note: Passive, past simple: was + past participle.

rounds.prompt: By the time we finally found the cinema, the film ___ already started.
rounds.note: Past perfect: finished before another past action.

rounds.prompt: A new bridge has ___ built across the river to reduce traffic in the town centre.
rounds.note: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle.

rounds.prompt: The names of the winners will ___ announced at the end of the ceremony.
rounds.note: Future passive: will be + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Most teenagers hate ___ told what to do, especially by their parents.
rounds.note: Passive gerund: being + past participle, after verbs like hate and avoid.

rounds.prompt: I ___ not realise how late it was until I looked at my phone and saw five missed calls.
rounds.note: Past simple negative: did not + base verb.

rounds.prompt: Leo enjoys swimming, and so ___ his younger brother, who trains every morning before school.
rounds.note: So + auxiliary + subject. Enjoys → so does.

rounds.prompt: My grandfather ___ to be a fisherman before he opened his restaurant by the harbour.
rounds.note: Used to for past states. Would cannot be used for states like be.

rounds.prompt: It ___ have been Tom who called you this morning. He is on a plane to Brazil right now.
rounds.note: Cannot have + past participle: you are sure it was impossible.

rounds.prompt: I should ___ listened to my parents when they told me to start revising earlier.
rounds.note: Should have + past participle: a past mistake.

rounds.prompt: The restaurant was so busy yesterday that we ___ to wait an hour for a table.
rounds.note: The past of have to is had to. Must has no past form.

rounds.prompt: All the players ___ been asked to bring their passports, so please check that you have yours.
rounds.note: Present perfect passive with a plural subject: have been asked.

rounds.prompt: By this time next year, I ___ have finished my degree and started my first job.
rounds.note: Future perfect: will have + past participle.

rounds.prompt: Little ___ she know that her friends had organised a surprise party for her.
rounds.note: Negative adverbials such as little, never and hardly are followed by inversion.

rounds.prompt: The tickets sold out in less than an hour, and so ___ the extra dates they added the next day.
rounds.note: So + auxiliary + subject. Sold → so did.

rounds.prompt: ___ I known about the strike, I would have taken a taxi to the airport.
rounds.note: Had I known = If I had known. The inversion replaces if.

rounds.prompt: When we were children, our grandmother ___ tell us a story every night before bed.
rounds.note: Would for repeated past actions. (Used would need two words: used to tell.)

rounds.prompt: I would rather ___ go to the party if Lucy is not going to be there.
rounds.note: Would rather + not + base verb.

rounds.prompt: You did not need to bring a present — but it is lovely, thank you! You really should not ___.
rounds.note: Should not have (brought it): the participle is left out because it is clear.

rounds.prompt: The student ___ sits next to me in maths has just moved here from Canada.
rounds.note: Who (or that) for people as the subject.

rounds.prompt: We had a long chat with a neighbour ___ son plays for the national team.
rounds.note: Whose shows possession.

rounds.prompt: Sintra is the town ___ my parents first met, so we go back there every summer.
rounds.note: Where for places, when a full clause follows.

rounds.prompt: Our flight was cancelled at the last minute, ___ meant we had to spend the night at the airport.
rounds.note: Which after a comma refers back to the whole idea before it.

rounds.prompt: I will never forget the day ___ I passed my driving test. I drove around for hours!
rounds.note: When for times.

rounds.prompt: Nobody showed Tom how to play the guitar; he taught ___ by watching videos online.
rounds.note: Reflexive pronoun: the subject and the object are the same person.

rounds.prompt: Did you two enjoy ___ at the festival? You both look exhausted!
rounds.note: Enjoy + reflexive pronoun. You two → yourselves.

rounds.prompt: Although they live on opposite sides of the world, the two cousins speak to each ___ every day.
rounds.note: Each other: a reciprocal pronoun.

rounds.prompt: ___ is often said that first impressions are the ones that count.
rounds.note: It is said that … : it stands for the that-clause.

rounds.prompt: ___ used to be a cinema on this corner, but it closed down when I was a child.
rounds.note: There + be introduces something that existed.

rounds.prompt: My laptop finally stopped working last week, so I have had to buy a new ___.
rounds.note: One replaces a countable noun when it is a different thing.

rounds.prompt: The museum, ___ opened in 1998, attracts thousands of visitors every year.
rounds.note: After a comma (non-defining clause) use which, not that.

rounds.prompt: The receptionist to ___ I spoke was extremely helpful and found us a better room.
rounds.note: Preposition + whom for people.

rounds.prompt: ___ surprised me most about the city was how friendly everyone was.
rounds.note: What means the thing that.

rounds.prompt: I felt so ill that I did not eat ___ for the whole day.
rounds.note: Anything in negative sentences. Nothing would make a double negative.

rounds.prompt: Group projects are popular with students because they allow ___ to learn from each other.
rounds.note: Object pronoun after allow.

rounds.prompt: The city is famous for ___ ancient walls, which were built by the Romans.
rounds.note: Its, with no apostrophe, is the possessive of it.

rounds.prompt: I find ___ difficult to concentrate when there is music playing in the background.
rounds.note: Find it + adjective + to-infinitive: it stands for the infinitive.

rounds.prompt: Of all the films I saw this year, the ___ I enjoyed most was a small Iranian drama.
rounds.note: The one = the film.

rounds.prompt: Nobody really knows ___ happened to the ship after it left the harbour in 1872.
rounds.note: What = the thing that.

rounds.prompt: Now that she is eighteen, Ana would love a flat of her ___.
rounds.note: Of your own.

rounds.prompt: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up by Friday.
rounds.note: Anyone who … : who for people.

rounds.prompt: I would appreciate ___ if you could reply by the end of the week.
rounds.note: Appreciate it if … : it stands for the if-clause.

rounds.prompt: Many of the people ___ I interviewed had never travelled abroad.
rounds.note: Object of the relative clause: whom, who or that.

rounds.prompt: Can you get some milk on your way home? There is not ___ left in the fridge.
rounds.note: Not any: any in negatives. Milk is uncountable.

rounds.prompt: Very ___ people turned up to the meeting, so it was postponed until next week.
rounds.note: Very few + countable noun: almost none.

rounds.prompt: We do not have ___ time left, so let us focus on the most important points.
rounds.note: Much with uncountable nouns in negatives.

rounds.prompt: I tried both of the shortcuts you suggested, but ___ of them worked.
rounds.note: Neither is for two things.

rounds.prompt: I invited six friends to my party, but ___ of them could come, so I celebrated with my family instead.
rounds.note: None is for more than two.

rounds.prompt: At sixteen, you are not old ___ to vote, but you can get a part-time job.
rounds.note: Enough comes after the adjective.

rounds.prompt: We visited four countries in two weeks, and ___ one was completely different from the last.
rounds.note: Each or every + one, for the members of a group taken separately.

rounds.prompt: We have not quite finished the exercise. Could we have ___ ten minutes, please?
rounds.note: Another + number + plural noun means that many more.

rounds.prompt: Some people relax by doing sport, while ___ prefer to read or watch films.
rounds.note: Others means other people. No noun follows.

rounds.prompt: I have two brothers, and ___ of them work in IT, like my father.
rounds.note: Both of + plural pronoun, for two people.

rounds.prompt: I spent the ___ weekend revising for my biology exam, so I did not go out once.
rounds.note: The whole + singular noun.

rounds.prompt: It rained ___ day yesterday, so we stayed indoors and played board games.
rounds.note: All day means from morning to night.

rounds.prompt: Who would you say is ___ best player in your team at the moment?
rounds.note: The before a superlative.

rounds.prompt: Hardly ___ students signed up for the trip, so the school had to cancel it.
rounds.note: Hardly any means almost none.

rounds.prompt: There is not ___ point in complaining now; the decision has already been made.
rounds.note: Not much or not any with uncountable nouns.

rounds.prompt: I have made ___ few friends since I moved here, so I do not feel lonely any more.
rounds.note: A few is positive (some). Few alone is negative (hardly any).

rounds.prompt: ___ four years, the Olympic Games are held in a different country.
rounds.note: Every + number + plural noun for regular intervals.

rounds.prompt: I have ___ idea where I left my keys. Have you seen them anywhere?
rounds.note: No idea. Not and none cannot go directly before a noun.

rounds.prompt: The buses run ___ twenty minutes during the week, but less often at weekends.
rounds.note: Every + number + plural noun for regular intervals.

rounds.prompt: After ___ the effort she had put into her project, she deserved to win first prize.
rounds.note: All the + noun.

rounds.prompt: Most ___ the people I spoke to at the conference had travelled from abroad.
rounds.note: Most of the + plural noun.

rounds.prompt: Once ___ week, the whole family gets together for lunch at my grandmother’s house.
rounds.note: Once a week: a means each here.

rounds.prompt: The two teams scored three goals ___, so the match went to penalties.
rounds.note: Each after a number: three goals for every team.

rounds.prompt: There is ___ doubt that the internet has changed the way we learn.
rounds.note: There is no doubt that … .

rounds.prompt: Martin was ___ tired after the night shift that he fell asleep on the bus home.
rounds.note: So + adjective + that + result.

rounds.prompt: It was ___ a beautiful evening that we decided to eat outside.
rounds.note: Such + a + adjective + noun + that + result.

rounds.prompt: I was far ___ shocked by the news to say anything at all.
rounds.note: Too + adjective + to-infinitive.

rounds.prompt: The concert was far better ___ any of us had expected.
rounds.note: Comparative + than. Watch the spelling: than, not then.

rounds.prompt: My new phone is not nearly as fast ___ my old one was, which is really frustrating.
rounds.note: Not (nearly) as + adjective + as.

rounds.prompt: The more you practise speaking, ___ more confident you will feel in the exam.
rounds.note: The + comparative, the + comparative.

rounds.prompt: The longer we waited for news, the ___ anxious we became.
rounds.note: The + comparative, the + comparative. Anxious takes more.

rounds.prompt: This is by far the ___ challenging course I have ever taken.
rounds.note: By far + superlative.

rounds.prompt: The new model is ___ more expensive than the old one, but it is also much faster.
rounds.note: Much, far, even or still can strengthen a comparative. Very cannot.

rounds.prompt: No sooner had we sat down at our table ___ the waiter brought us the menu.
rounds.note: No sooner … than. Hardly … when is the matching pair.

rounds.prompt: Doctors recommend that we eat ___ sugar and more vegetables.
rounds.note: Less with uncountable nouns. Fewer is for countable nouns.

rounds.prompt: There were so ___ people at the concert that we could hardly move.
rounds.note: So many + countable noun + that + result.

rounds.prompt: The film was so long ___ half the audience had fallen asleep before the end.
rounds.note: So + adjective + that + result.

rounds.prompt: Try to get here as early ___ you can — the best seats go very quickly.
rounds.note: As + adverb + as you can.

rounds.prompt: It took me a while, but I eventually got used ___ driving on the left.
rounds.note: Get used to + -ing.

rounds.prompt: To be honest, I would rather stay at home ___ go out in this weather.
rounds.note: Would rather … than.

rounds.prompt: As far ___ I am concerned, the new timetable is a big improvement.
rounds.note: As far as I am concerned: in my opinion.

rounds.prompt: Maria has been working at the hospital ___ she finished her degree in 2019.
rounds.note: Since + the starting point, with the present perfect.

rounds.prompt: I am sure he did not break your phone ___ purpose; it just slipped out of his hand.
rounds.note: On purpose = deliberately.

rounds.prompt: Could you look ___ my cat while I am on holiday? She only needs feeding twice a day.
rounds.note: Look after = take care of.

rounds.prompt: The outdoor concert was called ___ at the last minute because of a storm warning.
rounds.note: Call off = cancel.

rounds.prompt: She grew ___ in a small fishing village, which is why she still loves the sea.
rounds.note: Grow up.

rounds.prompt: We ran ___ of petrol on the motorway and had to walk two kilometres to a garage.
rounds.note: Run out of = have none left.

rounds.prompt: We set ___ at dawn so that we would reach the top of the mountain before midday.
rounds.note: Set off (or out) = start a journey.

rounds.prompt: Scientists have carried ___ a series of tests on the new vaccine, and the results are promising.
rounds.note: Carry out tests, research, a survey.

rounds.prompt: Although the forecast was terrible, the weather turned ___ to be perfect for our picnic.
rounds.note: Turn out to be = prove to be in the end.

rounds.prompt: After years of trying, my uncle finally managed to give ___ smoking.
rounds.note: Give up = stop doing.

rounds.prompt: While tidying the attic, I came ___ some old photos of my grandparents’ wedding.
rounds.note: Come across = find by chance.

rounds.prompt: Could you find ___ what time the museum opens on Sundays?
rounds.note: Find out = discover information.

rounds.prompt: If you keep spending money like that, you will end ___ with nothing left by the end of the month.
rounds.note: End up = find yourself in a situation at the end.

rounds.prompt: The manager promised to deal ___ our complaint as soon as possible.
rounds.note: Deal with.

rounds.prompt: I get ___ really well with my new flatmates, which makes sharing a kitchen much easier.
rounds.note: Get on (or along) with someone.

rounds.prompt: Nothing can make ___ for all the time we lost while the train was delayed.
rounds.note: Make up for = compensate for.

rounds.prompt: I cannot put up ___ this noise any longer — I am going to speak to the neighbours.
rounds.note: Put up with = tolerate.

rounds.prompt: The train is quicker. ___ the other hand, the bus is much cheaper.
rounds.note: On the other hand introduces the opposite point.

rounds.prompt: We talked about going away for the weekend, but in the ___ we decided to stay at home.
rounds.note: In the end = finally, after some time.

rounds.prompt: ___ first, I found the city overwhelming, but after a few weeks I felt completely at home.
rounds.note: At first = in the beginning (before a change).

rounds.prompt: The factory closed last year. ___ a result, hundreds of people lost their jobs.
rounds.note: As a result.

rounds.prompt: There were a few problems with the hotel, but ___ the whole we had a wonderful holiday.
rounds.note: On the whole = generally.

rounds.prompt: ___ the way, did you remember to buy the tickets for Saturday?
rounds.note: By the way introduces a new topic.

rounds.prompt: I cannot come to the party. I have too much work and, ___ any case, I do not really feel well.
rounds.note: In any case = anyway.

rounds.prompt: You are welcome to stay with us ___ the time being, until you find a flat of your own.
rounds.note: For the time being = for now.

rounds.prompt: Your table will be ready in about ten minutes. ___ the meantime, can I get you something to drink?
rounds.note: In the meantime = while you wait.

rounds.prompt: Some birds, ___ instance, can sleep while they are flying.
rounds.note: For instance = for example.

rounds.prompt: I am so sorry about your vase. I knocked it over ___ accident when I was cleaning.
rounds.note: By accident = not on purpose.

rounds.prompt: The students were made ___ rewrite the whole essay because they had copied it from the internet.
rounds.note: Passive of make takes a to-infinitive.

rounds.prompt: My brother suggested ___ we should leave early to avoid the traffic.
rounds.note: Suggest that + clause (never suggest to do).

rounds.prompt: She finally admitted that it ___ been her who broke the window.
rounds.note: Reported past: it had been her.

rounds.prompt: The new president is said ___ be very popular with young voters.
rounds.note: Be said to + infinitive.

rounds.prompt: My parents have always encouraged me ___ follow my dreams, even when they seemed unrealistic.
rounds.note: Encourage someone to do something.

rounds.prompt: He promised me ___ he would never be late again — but he was late the very next day.
rounds.note: Promise (someone) that + clause.

rounds.prompt: We left very early so ___ not to get stuck in the rush-hour traffic.
rounds.note: So as not to + infinitive: negative purpose.

rounds.prompt: Please do not hesitate ___ contact me if you have any questions.
rounds.note: Hesitate to do something.

rounds.prompt: Personally, I prefer spending time outdoors ___ sitting in front of a screen.
rounds.note: Prefer A to B.

rounds.prompt: Even though we offered to split the bill, he insisted ___ paying for everyone.
rounds.note: Insist on + -ing.

rounds.prompt: The room had nothing ___ a small bed and a broken lamp, so we left the next morning.
rounds.note: Nothing but = only.

rounds.prompt: The trip was ___ from perfect: it rained every day and our luggage got lost.
rounds.note: Far from perfect = not at all perfect.

rounds.prompt: I did not enjoy the film ___ all; in fact, I left before the end.
rounds.note: Not … at all = not in any way.

rounds.prompt: Do not worry about the money. You can pay me back ___ you like — there is no hurry.
rounds.note: Whenever = at any time.

rounds.prompt: She told us she had never been abroad, ___ surprised everyone in the class.
rounds.note: Which after a comma refers back to the whole idea.

rounds.prompt: The village, ___ can only be reached by boat, has fewer than a hundred inhabitants.
rounds.note: Non-defining clause about a thing: which, never that.

rounds.prompt: The main reason for ___ I chose this university was its excellent library.
rounds.note: Preposition + which for things.

rounds.prompt: We stayed in a small hotel, the owner of ___ was a retired chef.
rounds.note: The owner of which = whose owner.

rounds.prompt: ___ I like most about living by the sea is the fresh air in the morning.
rounds.note: What = the thing that.

rounds.prompt: I cannot believe ___ a mess the children have made of the kitchen!
rounds.note: What + a + noun in exclamations.

rounds.prompt: No matter ___ you decide, I will support you.
rounds.note: No matter what = whatever.

rounds.prompt: Will the weather be good enough for the picnic? I hope ___ — we have already bought all the food.
rounds.note: I hope so: so replaces the clause.

rounds.prompt: I have ___ much homework this week that I have not had time to go out at all.
rounds.note: So much + uncountable noun + that.

rounds.prompt: Is this ___ first time you have been to Lisbon? You seem to know your way around.
rounds.note: The first time + present perfect.

rounds.prompt: ___ older I get, the more I appreciate my parents’ advice.
rounds.note: The + comparative, the + comparative.

rounds.prompt: Regular exercise is ___ of the best ways to reduce stress.
rounds.note: One of the + superlative + plural noun.

rounds.prompt: Thank you for ___ your help with the move; I could not have done it without you.
rounds.note: All + possessive + noun.

rounds.prompt: What ___ beautiful view! I could sit here for hours.
rounds.note: What a + adjective + singular noun.

rounds.prompt: She burst ___ tears when she heard that she had won the scholarship.
rounds.note: Burst into tears / laughter.
